description: gproxy is a Rust-based multi-channel LLM proxy that exposes OpenAI / Claude / Gemini-style APIs through a unified gateway, with a built-in admin console, user/key management, and request/usage auditing.

latest_release.name: gproxy v4.3.0
latest_release.body:
## v4.3.0

> GPROXY now fronts MCP servers, and adds the Factory Droid channel. The full gateway is native-only: Cloudflare Workers, Netlify and Vercel run the new single-tenant engine `gproxy-lite`, and the edge and serverless builds of the full gateway are removed. Running SSE streams receive heartbeats while they are quiet.
>
> GPROXY 现在可以代理 MCP 服务器，并新增 Factory Droid 渠道。完整的网关只支持原生目标：Cloudflare Workers、Netlify 和 Vercel 改为运行新的单租户引擎 `gproxy-lite`，完整网关的 edge 与 serverless 构建已移除。流式响应静默时会收到心跳。

### English

#### Breaking: serverless platforms run `gproxy-lite`

This release removes deployment targets. Native, Docker, Render and Heroku deployments are not affected; Cloudflare Workers, Netlify and Vercel deployments must be set up again before upgrading.

- The Cloudflare Workers host (`gproxy-host-edge`) and its WebAssembly bundle (`gproxy-edge-cloudflare.zip`) are removed, together with the D1 store backend (`store.kind = "d1"`) and the `store` cache backend. A migration drops that cache's tables.
- The Cloudflare, Netlify and Vercel deployment templates and their deploy buttons are removed.
- The `gproxy-serverless` executable that the Netlify and Vercel templates ran is removed, together with its release archives (`gproxy-serverless-linux-<arch>-musl.zip`).
- Those platforms now run `gproxy-lite`, from the templates in `deploy/lite`. See [Cloudflare Workers, Netlify, and Vercel](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/deployment/lite). It has every channel, including the ones that sign in with OAuth, and every HTTP operation with protocol conversion, in a WebAssembly module of 10.7 MB (the old Workers bundle was 27 MB).
- `gproxy-lite` is single-tenant and has no database. It lacks users, organizations, teams, API keys and permissions (one access key admits every request); budgets, quotas, pricing, usage records, rate limits and the audit log; several credentials per provider; routes, aliases and tiers; rewrite rules; the console and the management API; MCP; a local model catalogue and tokenizer. Its configuration is one JSON document in `GPROXY_LITE_CONFIG`, and its state is one key-value store per deployment: a Durable Object on Cloudflare, Netlify Blobs on Netlify, Upstash Redis on Vercel. Credentials are renewed before a request, after a 401 and on a schedule.
- It does not read a v4.2 database. A former deployment is set up again from its providers and credentials; OAuth channels sign in again through `/lite/login/start`.
- If you need what `gproxy-lite` lacks, move to the container deployment: Docker on your own host, or the Render or Heroku template, with PostgreSQL. See [Docker, Render, and Heroku](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/deployment/containers). Netlify and Vercel deployments already use PostgreSQL, so they can keep their database. The native binary does not open a D1 database, so a former Workers deployment starts on a new one.
- The templates build from source (`sh deploy/lite/build.sh`); there are no deploy buttons and no prebuilt release archive yet.
- The stateless crates `gproxy-protocol`, `gproxy-client`, `gproxy-client-sdk`, `gproxy-upstream`, `gproxy-channel`, `gproxy-convert` and `gproxy-lite` build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and CI checks them on that target. The engine, the store, the app and the hosts no longer do.

#### MCP servers

GPROXY fronts MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, streamable HTTP) the way it fronts model providers. See [MCP servers](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/guides/mcp-servers).

- An administrator registers a server as a provider with the channel `mcp` and its endpoint as the base URL. Users, teams and organizations sign in to it with OAuth, a pasted secret or nothing; GPROXY keeps the sign-in alive. A tool call never uses another person's credential.
- A client needs only a URL and a gateway API key. A client that cannot do OAuth itself needs no change.
- Two addresses: `/connect/mcp/<name>` is one server with its own tool names, and `/connect/mcp` aggregates every server the caller can us

detail.readme: # GPROXY [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/LeenHawk/gproxy)](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/latest) [![CI](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](LICENSE) [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/custom%2B37316%2Fgithub.com%2FLeenHawk%2Fgproxy.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/custom%2B37316%2Fgithub.com%2FLeenHawk%2Fgproxy?ref=badge_shield) [Documentation](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/) · [Downloads](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases) · [Discussions](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/discussions) · [Sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/LeenHawk) GPROXY is a self-hosted gateway for LLM APIs, written in Rust. You hand it your upstream accounts: API keys, the OAuth logins behind subscriptions such as Claude Code or Codex, or browser cookies. The people who use it get one base URL, one GPROXY API key and model names that you choose. They never see the upstream secrets. GPROXY does not run models. Inference is done by the upstream service. The full manual is at ****. ![The console's provider page](.github/readme/providers-en.webp) ## When it is useful - You have a few Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions and a pile of API keys, and you want to share them with a team or with friends. Everyone gets a key of their own with its own permissions, rate limits and budget, and you can see afterwards who used what. - The same model is available from several sources and you want them to back each other up. When an account is rate-limited or fails, the request moves to the next one and the client does not need to know. - The client only speaks the OpenAI format and the upstream is Claude or Gemini, or the other way round. - The gateway has to stay up on a server, a NAS or in a container. If all you want is to switch models for Claude Code or Codex on your own computer, a desktop switcher is less work. GPROXY does not edit those tools' configuration files; you enter the gateway URL and key yourself. ## Features ### Subscription accounts as upstreams Besides API keys, GPROXY can use subscription accounts as upstreams: Claude Code, Claude on the web, Codex (a ChatGPT account), Gemini CLI, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kiro, Grok Build, Kimi Code, Trae, Devin, WorkBuddy and others. You sign in once in the console and GPROXY refreshes the tokens from then on. A provider can hold several accounts. You can look up each account's quota windows, and an account that the upstream has rate-limited gives way to the others. With session affinity turned on, a conversation stays on one account, so the prompt cache is not lost by switching accounts. Claude Code and Codex CLI send more than model requests. They also ask for account details, usage, plugins and so on. GPROXY answers these too, so the official CLIs work when pointed at the gateway. What the CLI shows is the caller's own usage on the gateway; nothing about the shared account is disclosed to them. ### Several users Accounts are organized into users, organizations and teams, and an administrator can be limited to one organization or team. Each key can be restricted to certain providers and models and given rate limits and a spending budget. A credential can belong to a user, an organization or a team, and nobody else can use it. Tools that sign in with OAuth, such as Claude Code and Codex CLI, can sign in to your GPROXY instance directly, so you do not have to hand out a key to each person. Every upstream call is recorded with its token counts and cost. There are also request logs and an audit log. ### Protocol conversion Clients can use OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Claude Messages or Gemini GenerateContent, streaming or not. When the client and the upstream use different formats, the gateway converts between them. Embeddings, rerank, images, audio, video, files and Realtime are available where the upstream offers them. Conversion changes only the format of a request. A model that cannot call tools or read images still cannot when it is asked in another format. ### Model routes Clients ask for a name such as `fast` or `coding`, and you decide which providers and upstream models serve it. Route members can be put in tiers; a later tier is used only when nothing in the earlier ones is available. Within a tier, requests are spread round-robin, by weight, or in a fixed order. You can also do without routes and ask for `provider/model` directly. ![The console's model route page](.github/readme/routes-en.webp) ### Rewrite rules Requests and responses can be rewritten per provider: system prompts, JSON fields, regular-expression replacements, headers and prompt-cache breakpoints. Some clients cannot set cache fields. For those, you can put an agreed string in the prompt, and when the provider has the option turned on, GPROXY replaces it with a cache breakpoint. ### Channels Apart from the subscription channels above, the built-in channels include OpenAI, Claude API, Google AI Studio, Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, DashScope, Volcengine, xAI, NVIDIA NIM and others; the [provider guide](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/guides/providers) has the full list. A compatible service that differs only in its address and headers can be added with the `custom` channel. When a service needs an adapter of its own, you can write a channel plugin outside this repository, without forking, as described in [Adding a channel](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/development/adding-a-channel). ### Ways to run it - A native server: the CLI for Linux, macOS and Windows with the web console built in, or a headless build without the console. - A container. - A desktop and mobile app with the console and a setup wizard built in. - A Rust library: embed it in your own program through `gproxy-sdk`. The database can be SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. ## Installing On Linux and macOS: ```sh curl -fsSL https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell irm https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/install.ps1 | iex ``` The script downloads the latest stable CLI, asks a few questions (data directory, port, administrator password) and can register a background service. Run it with `--help` to see the options, for example `--edition headless` for a build without the web console. With [Homebrew](https://github.com/LeenHawk/homebrew-tap) on macOS or Linux: ```sh brew install leenhawk/tap/gproxy # or gproxy-headless brew install --cask leenhawk/tap/gproxy-desktop # desktop app, macOS only ``` `brew services start gproxy` runs it in the background. You can also download a package by hand from [Releases](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/latest). Each release contains: - `gproxy-*`: the CLI with the web console built in; - `gproxy-headless-*`: the CLI without the console, for CI and small servers; - `gproxy-tauri-*`: the desktop and mobile application. GPROXY Desktop, CLI and Headless are also on the Microsoft Store ([Desktop](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P2FJRB9RS4Z), [CLI](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NBMH3S5K0L9), [Headless](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9ND7FQQMV566)), and the Android app is on [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.leenhawk.gproxy.desktop/). macOS builds are not notarized. The [download page](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/download) lists every platform and its requirements. Stable releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`. The `staging` and `nightly` releases are the beta and development channels. ## Getting started Start the server with a data directory: ```sh ./gproxy serve --data-dir ./data --port 8787 ``` The first time it runs in a terminal it asks a few setup questions. Without a terminal it creates an administrator account and prints the password and a gateway API key; save both. By default it listens on 127.0.0.1 and keeps its SQLite database in `./data/gproxy.db`. Set `GPROXY_MASTER_KEY` before you add any upstream credentials. Without it, upstream secrets are stored unencrypted. Keep the key and the data directory together when you move or upgrade the instance; see [Configuration](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/reference/configuration). Then open and: 1. Under **Providers**, add a provider (for example `openai-main` on the `openai` channel) and its API key, and test the credential. 2. Under **Model routes**, create a route named `fast` with that provider and the model you tested as its member. Now any OpenAI-compatible client can use it with the gateway API key: ```sh export GPROXY_KEY='your-gproxy-api-key' curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GPROXY_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"fast","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' ``` The same route answers Claude (`/v1/messages`) and Gemini (`/v1beta/models/fast:generateContent`) requests. The [tutorial](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/getting-started/quick-start) goes through this step by step, and [CLI clients](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/guides/cli-clients) shows how to point Codex CLI and Claude Code at the gateway. The desktop and mobile app runs the same steps as a setup wizard and has the console built in. ## Hosted deployment The Render and Heroku buttons at the top of this page run the native binary in a small container with PostgreSQL. You will be asked for an administrator password and a master key. Read [Docker, Render and Heroku](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/deployment/containers) first; it covers database choice, plan costs and the limits of each platform. Cloudflare Workers, Netlify and Vercel run `gproxy-lite` instead: a single-tenant engine with one access key and no database, built from the same channels and protocol conversion. Their buttons deploy the templates in `deploy/lite` with a prebuilt engine from the `staging` release, which follows `main`; nothing is compiled. You will be asked for `GPROXY_LITE_CONFIG`, the configuration JSON. See [Cloudflare Workers, Netlify, and Vercel](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/deployment/lite). ## Upgrading from v3 Stop v3 and back up its database, master key and startup configuration. Then start v4 with the same configuration. SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL databases are migrated on first start; accounts, passwords, API keys and usage history are kept, and anything that could not be mapped is listed in the migration report. Do not run v3 and v4 against the same database at the same time. Details are in [Migrating v3 to v4](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/deployment/v3-to-v4). ## Performance Measured with the [v4.0.0 Linux x86_64 release](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/tag/v4.0.0) on a Ryzen 7 8745H (8 cores, 16 threads), SQLite on NVMe, with the load generator (`oha 1.16.0`), the gateway and a mock upstream on the same machine. Requests were non-streaming Chat Completions passing through authentication, routing, usage extraction, pricing and persistence. The mock returned 25 input and 18 output tokens with no delay. Body logging was off; usage recording and cost settlement were on. Each figure is the median of three 10-second runs after a 2-second warm-up. | Request logs | Connections | Requests/s | p50 | p99 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Off | 1 | 2,882 | 0.34 ms | 0.50 ms | | Off | 32 | 28,303 | 0.76 ms | 2.71 ms | | Off | 64 | 27,263 | 1.47 ms | 41.91 ms | | Upstream and downstream metadata | 64 | 7,765 | 2.81 ms | 45.16 ms | With one connection the gateway adds about 0.30 ms to the median latency of calling the mock directly. All 1,989,395 requests returned 200, and the stored usage rows matched the request count with correct tokens and cost. Throughput stops growing at around 64 connections, where p99 rises to about 42 ms. These numbers are for short responses, same-protocol forwarding and local SQLite; measure your own workload if it involves long streams, protocol conversion, a remote database or real upstreams. ## Building from source You need stable Rust, Go and Clang, and for the console Node.js 22.12 or later and pnpm. The console has to be built before the binary, otherwise the binary has no console to serve: ```sh pnpm --dir console install --frozen-lockfile pnpm --dir console build cargo run -p gproxy -- serve ``` [Building from source](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/development/building) covers the headless build, the desktop app and the checks CI runs. Contributors should also read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Architecture](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/development/architecture); to add an upstream, see [Adding a channel](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/development/adding-a-channel). ## Reporting bugs Use [Issues](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/issues) for bugs and [Discussions](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/discussions) for questions. For anything you would rather not post publicly, email [leenhawk@leenhawk.com](mailto:leenhawk@leenhawk.com). Report security problems privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License GPROXY is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later; see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The library crates `gproxy-protocol`, `gproxy-protocol-macros`, `gproxy-client`, `gproxy-client-sdk`, `gproxy-cache`, `gproxy-file`, `gproxy-seaorm`, `gproxy-store` and `gproxy-tokenizer` are MIT-licensed; each has its own license file. ## Powered by         ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=LeenHawk/gproxy&type=Date)](https://www.star-history.com/#LeenHawk/gproxy&Date)
detail.readme_zh: # GPROXY [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/LeenHawk/gproxy)](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/latest) [![CI](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](LICENSE) [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/custom%2B37316%2Fgithub.com%2FLeenHawk%2Fgproxy.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/custom%2B37316%2Fgithub.com%2FLeenHawk%2Fgproxy?ref=badge_shield) [文档](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/) · [下载](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases) · [讨论](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/discussions) · [赞助](https://github.com/sponsors/LeenHawk) GPROXY 是一个自己部署的大模型 API 网关，用 Rust 写的。你把手里的上游账号交给它保管：API Key、Claude Code 或 Codex 这类订阅的 OAuth 登录、浏览器 Cookie 都可以。用的人只拿到一个网关地址、一把 GPROXY 的 Key 和你起的模型名，上游的密钥他们接触不到。 GPROXY 本身不运行模型，推理由上游服务完成。 完整文档：**** ![控制台的供应商页面](.github/readme/providers-zh-CN.webp) ## 什么情况下用得上 - 手里有几个 Claude、ChatGPT 订阅和一堆 API Key，想分给团队或朋友用。每人一把 Key，各有各的权限、限流和预算，谁用了多少事后能查到。 - 同一个模型有好几个来源，想让它们互为备份。某个账号被限流或者出错时，请求自动换到下一个，客户端不需要知道。 - 客户端只支持 OpenAI 格式，上游却是 Claude 或 Gemini，或者反过来。 - 网关要长期运行在服务器、NAS 或容器里。 如果只是想在自己电脑上给 Claude Code、Codex 这些工具换个模型，桌面上的切换工具更省事。GPROXY 不会替你修改这些工具的配置文件，网关地址和 Key 需要自己填。 ## 功能 ### 订阅账号做上游 除了各家的 API Key，GPROXY 还能把订阅账号当作上游：Claude Code、Claude 网页版、Codex（ChatGPT 账号）、Gemini CLI、Antigravity、GitHub Copilot CLI、Kiro、Grok Build、Kimi Code、Trae、Devin、WorkBuddy 等。在控制台里登录一次，之后令牌由 GPROXY 自动刷新。 一个供应商下可以放多个账号。每个账号的额度窗口可以查到，被上游限流的账号会先让给其他账号。打开会话亲和后，同一个对话固定使用同一个账号，提示缓存不会因为换号而失效。 Claude Code 和 Codex CLI 除了发模型请求，还会查询账号资料、用量、插件等信息。GPROXY 也处理这些请求，所以官方 CLI 指向网关后可以正常使用。CLI 里显示的是调用者自己在网关上的用量，共享账号的信息不会泄露给他。 ### 多人使用 账户分为用户、组织和团队，管理员可以只管某个组织或团队。每把 Key 可以限定能用的供应商和模型，并设置限流和费用预算。凭证可以归属于某个用户、组织或团队，其他人用不到。 Claude Code、Codex CLI 这类用 OAuth 登录的工具，可以直接登录到你的 GPROXY 实例，不必给每个人单独发 Key。 每次上游调用都会记一条用量，包含 token 数和费用。另有请求日志和审计日志。 ### 协议转换 对客户端提供 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses、Claude Messages 和 Gemini GenerateContent 四种接口，流式和非流式都支持。客户端与上游格式不同时由网关转换。嵌入、重排、图像、音频、视频、文件和 Realtime 接口在上游提供时同样可用。 转换只改变请求格式。上游模型不支持工具调用或图像输入时，换一种格式请求也仍然不支持。 ### 模型路由 客户端请求 `fast`、`coding` 这样的名字，背后用哪些供应商和上游模型由你决定。路由成员可以分层，前一层都不可用时才使用后一层；同一层内可以轮询、按权重分配或按固定顺序。不建路由也可以，直接用 `供应商/模型` 请求。 ![控制台的模型路由页面](.github/readme/routes-zh-CN.webp) ### 重写规则 可以按供应商改写请求和响应：系统提示词、JSON 字段、正则替换、请求头和提示缓存断点。有些客户端无法设置缓存字段，这时可以在提示词里写一个约定的字符串，供应商开启该选项后，GPROXY 会把它换成缓存断点。 ### 渠道 除上面的订阅类渠道外，内置渠道还有 OpenAI、Claude API、Google AI Studio、Vertex AI、AWS Bedrock、Azure、OpenRouter、DeepSeek、智谱 GLM、Kimi、MiniMax、阿里云百炼（DashScope）、火山方舟、xAI、NVIDIA NIM 等，完整列表见[供应商与凭证](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/guides/providers)。只是地址和请求头不同的兼容服务，用 `custom` 渠道填写地址即可接入。需要专用适配时，可以按[添加渠道](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/development/adding-a-channel)在仓库外写一个渠道插件，不必 fork。 ### 运行方式 - 原生服务：Linux、macOS 和 Windows 上的 CLI，内置 Web 控制台，也有不带控制台的 headless 版本。 - 容器。 - 桌面和手机应用，内置控制台和设置向导。 - Rust 库：通过 `gproxy-sdk` 嵌入自己的程序。 数据库支持 SQLite、PostgreSQL 和 MySQL。 ## 安装 Linux 和 macOS： ```sh curl -fsSL https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/install.sh | sh ``` Windows（PowerShell）： ```powershell irm https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/install.ps1 | iex ``` 脚本会下载最新稳定版 CLI，询问数据目录、端口、管理员密码等几个问题，也可以顺便注册为后台服务。可用选项见 `--help`，例如 `--edition headless` 安装不带 Web 控制台的版本。中文环境默认从 CNB 镜像下载。 macOS 和 Linux 也可以用 [Homebrew](https://github.com/LeenHawk/homebrew-tap) 安装： ```sh brew install leenhawk/tap/gproxy # 或 gproxy-headless brew install --cask leenhawk/tap/gproxy-desktop # 桌面应用，仅 macOS ``` `brew services start gproxy` 可在后台运行。 也可以从 [Releases](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/latest) 手动下载。每个版本包含三类安装包： - `gproxy-*`：内置 Web 控制台的 CLI； - `gproxy-headless-*`：不含控制台的 CLI，适合 CI 和小型服务器； - `gproxy-tauri-*`：桌面与移动应用。 Microsoft Store 上架了 GPROXY Desktop、CLI 和 Headless（[Desktop](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9P2FJRB9RS4Z)、[CLI](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NBMH3S5K0L9)、[Headless](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9ND7FQQMV566)），Android 应用可以从 [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.leenhawk.gproxy.desktop/) 安装。macOS 版本没有经过公证。各平台的安装包和系统要求见[下载页](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/download)。 稳定版的标签形如 `vX.Y.Z`；`staging` 和 `nightly` 两个 Release 分别对应测试版和开发版更新通道。 ## 上手 指定数据目录启动服务： ```sh ./gproxy serve --data-dir ./data --port 8787 ``` 在终端里第一次运行时会先问几个设置问题。没有终端时，GPROXY 直接创建管理员账户，并打印管理员密码和一个网关 API Key，请把两者都保存好。默认只监听 127.0.0.1，SQLite 数据库位于 `./data/gproxy.db`。 添加任何上游凭证之前，先设置 `GPROXY_MASTER_KEY`；不设置的话，上游密钥会以明文保存。迁移或升级实例时，主密钥和数据目录要一起保留，详见[配置](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/reference/configuration)。 然后打开 ： 1. 在**供应商**页面添加一个供应商（例如 `openai` 渠道的 `openai-main`）和它的 API Key，并测试凭证。 2. 在**模型路由**页面新建名为 `fast` 的路由，把刚才的供应商和测试通过的模型添加为成员。 之后任何兼容 OpenAI 的客户端都可以用网关 API Key 调用： ```sh export GPROXY_KEY='your-gproxy-api-key' curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GPROXY_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"fast","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"你好"}]}' ``` 同一个路由也可以用 Claude（`/v1/messages`）和 Gemini（`/v1beta/models/fast:generateContent`）格式请求。[快速开始](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/getting-started/quick-start)一步步演示了上面的过程；Codex CLI 和 Claude Code 的接入方法见 [CLI 客户端](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/guides/cli-clients)。 桌面和手机应用把这些步骤做成了设置向导，控制台也内置在应用里。 ## 托管部署 页面顶部的 Render 和 Heroku 按钮在一个小容器里运行原生程序，数据库是 PostgreSQL。 部署时需要填写管理员密码和主密钥。动手之前请先读 [Docker、Render 与 Heroku](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/deployment/containers)，里面讲了数据库怎么选、各平台套餐的费用，以及平台本身的限制。 Cloudflare Workers、Netlify 和 Vercel 上运行的是 `gproxy-lite`：一个单租户引擎，只有一把访问密钥，不带数据库，使用同样的渠道和协议转换。这三个按钮部署 `deploy/lite` 里的模板，引擎是 `staging` 发布里预先构建好的（跟随 `main`），部署时不编译。部署时需要填写配置 JSON `GPROXY_LITE_CONFIG`。详见 [Cloudflare Workers、Netlify 与 Vercel](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/deployment/lite)。 ## 从 v3 升级 停止 v3，备份数据库、主密钥和启动配置，然后用同样的配置启动 v4。SQLite、PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 数据库会在首次启动时自动迁移，账户、密码、API Key 和历史用量都会保留，无法映射的配置会列在迁移报告里。不要让 v3 和 v4 同时连接同一个数据库。详见[从 v3 迁移到 v4](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/deployment/v3-to-v4)。 ## 性能 测试使用 [v4.0.0 Linux x86_64 正式版](https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/releases/tag/v4.0.0)，机器是 Ryzen 7 8745H（8 核 16 线程），SQLite 放在 NVMe 上；压测工具 `oha 1.16.0`、网关和模拟上游运行在同一台机器上。请求为非流式 Chat Completions，完整经过鉴权、路由、用量提取、计价和落库。模拟上游每次返回 25 个输入 token、18 个输出 token，不加延迟。测试时关闭了正文记录，用量记录和费用结算保持开启。每个数字取三轮测试的中位数，每轮先预热 2 秒，再测 10 秒。 | 请求日志 | 连接数 | 请求/秒 | p50 | p99 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 关闭 | 1 | 2,882 | 0.34 ms | 0.50 ms | | 关闭 | 32 | 28,303 | 0.76 ms | 2.71 ms | | 关闭 | 64 | 27,263 | 1.47 ms | 41.91 ms | | 记录上下游元数据 | 64 | 7,765 | 2.81 ms | 45.16 ms | 单连接时，经过网关比直接请求模拟上游的中位延迟多约 0.30 ms。全部 1,989,395 个请求都返回 200，落库的用量行数与请求数一致，token 和费用也都核对无误。连接数到 64 左右吞吐不再增长，p99 升到约 42 ms。以上结果只针对短响应、同协议转发和本地 SQLite；如果你的场景有长流式响应、协议转换、远程数据库或真实上游，请自己实测。 ## 从源码构建 需要 stable Rust、Go 和 Clang；构建控制台还需要 Node.js 22.12 或更高版本以及 pnpm。必须先构建控制台再构建程序，否则程序里没有控制台可用： ```sh pnpm --dir console install --frozen-lockfile pnpm --dir console build cargo run -p gproxy -- serve ``` Headless 版本和桌面应用的构建方法，以及 CI 跑的检查，见[从源码构建](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/development/building)。参与开发请先读 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) 和[架构](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/development/architecture)；要接入新的上游，见[添加渠道](https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/zh-cn/development/adding-a-channel)。 ##
